evidence.method: CSPICE spkpos('SUN', et, 'MOON_ME', 'CN+S', 'MOON'); unit vector; sub-point = planetocentric latitude/east longitude of the direction (the 1737.4 km sphere); angular radius = asin(R_body/|r|). MOON_ME resolves to MOON_ME_DE440_ME421.
assumptions: Moon-centred: from a surface point the direction differs by up to R_moon/range (≈ 2.4 arcsec for the Sun, ≈ 0.26° for the Earth); use the site ephemeris for topocentric values.
Sun radius 695700.0000 km from the loaded PCK.

limitations: Moon-centred direction: from a surface point the Sun's direction differs by at most R_moon / range (about 2.4 arcsec). Use the site ephemeris for topocentric azimuth and elevation.
Lighting the whole globe from this direction is the illumination of a smooth sphere; terrain shadows need the terrain horizon (POST /api/v1/analysis/timeline).
Apparent direction (light time and stellar aberration at the Moon's centre); gravitational light deflection is not modelled.
